raw_response_summary.all_returned_window_ends_capped_at: 2084-01-31 (no window in the response extends past this date, even though the queried date_range runs to 2085-06-01)

note: The chart's gochara sweep is materialized in decade slices up to birth+100y (era_slice_key g3_2074_2084, ending 2084-01-31 = the documented 2084 horizon ceiling for this chart born 1984-02-05). The query's date_range (2083-06-01..2085-06-01) straddles that horizon: the portion before 2084-01-31 is real, swept data; the portion after (2084-02-01..2085-06-01, ~16 months of the query) is silently absent. Because rows.length > 0, provenance_envelope.empty_reason is null (register_gochara_windows.ts computes empty_reason as `rows.length === 0 ? <explanation> : null` -- confirmed at platform-mcp/src/tools/retrieval/register_gochara_windows.ts line ~1429). There is no field anywhere in the response (coverage, provenance_envelope, judgment_flags) that discloses 'part of your requested date_range falls beyond this chart's swept horizon.' coverage.sweep_completeness reports substeps_committed=270 but explicitly states 'No total-planned-substep denominator is reported here' -- so a caller cannot even infer the horizon boundary from that field. Contrast with the fully-beyond-horizon case (date_range 2090-01-01..2091-01-01, see gochara_forecast_get__horizon_2084_fully_beyond.json) where the tool DOES supply an honest, explicit empty_reason with a caveat about unswept decades. The disclosure only fires when the WHOLE query is empty, not when it is partially truncated by the horizon -- an inconsistency in the density/honesty contract (CLAUDE.md SS N.6/N.7).
